title: Foundational small-strain elasticity verification
purpose: Verify basic solid-element kinematics, regional constitutive assembly, standard result projection, displacement control, and strong-boundary reactions rather than only a fixed-mesh displacement regression.
physics: two- and three-dimensional small-strain linear elasticity
references: Abaqus 2024 element verification: constant-strain patch tests
DOLFINx elasticity using algebraic multigrid demo

execution.evidence: Analytical constant-strain, regional series-bar, and named-reaction checks run in serial, with partition-independent reaction and projection checks under two MPI ranks.

observables: Three-dimensional constant strain and stress on every cell.
Named-boundary reaction resultant under displacement control.
Regional axial stress and strain in a two-material series bar.
Engineering-default U/S/E/MISES field names and processing metadata.
acceptance: A 3D displacement-only static step creates a valid zero external-force vector and exactly reproduces a constant diagonal strain patch.
Projected S and E fields reproduce the analytical isotropic constitutive response on every cell.
The named positive-face reaction equals analytical stress times area.
A two-region series bar retains continuous axial stress and the correct regional compliance.
The same named-boundary reaction contract is partition-independent under MPI.
One-call solve_result(output=...) writes engineering-default U, S, E, and MISES to one XDMF/HDF5 result; SENER is an explicit diagnostic request.
Projected field metadata states that DG0 values are cell averages without nodal extrapolation, interelement smoothing, or material-boundary averaging.
limitations: This contract covers continuum Lagrange solid fields, not beams, shells, mixed incompressible elements, contact, or axisymmetric kinematics.
Affine MPC, weak, and contact reactions require separate force definitions.
The next external linear-elasticity benchmark should be NAFEMS LE10 or an equivalently published geometry and stress target.
